problem: Zero-shot object navigation methods build language-grounded global semantic maps that misrepresent the real layout and accumulate errors, and rely on large general-purpose LLMs/VLMs that are computationally heavy and not specialized for navigation.
motivation: Humans pick exploration directions by combining semantic priors, viewing confidence and distance cost, then verify the goal. The paper argues that a lightweight, navigation-aligned vision-language model plus cost/benefit-aware maps can replace heavyweight LLM reasoning while remaining zero-shot.
key_idea: Replace the BLIP2/LLM frontier scorer of VLFM with a small prompt-tuned vision-language model (PEIA), fuse semantic, confidence and cost maps to select an optimal-benefit frontier, and verify the goal with detection, segmentation, VQA and reflection.
insight: A 0.122B model prompt-tuned on 0.33M COCO data matches or beats the 7.8B BLIP2-OPT scorer in SR and DTG on HM3D (55.90 vs 55.25 SR), but with lower SPL (29.06 vs 30.31). Removing RDV drops SR from 55.90 to 52.35 and raises NE from 10.10 to 18.70, so the VQA confirmation corrects detector errors. Removing pre-training costs 3.55 SR, so discrete-prompt pre-training carries the image-grounded knowledge.
method: Initial map and frontiers: top-down 2D map from depth and odometry; frontiers are midpoints of boundaries of the explored area; the agent first rotates in place to build the initial map.

Semantic Map: PEIA predicts masked-word probabilities from the RGB view and a prompt like 'There may be a <mask> in the front area', giving a per-pixel semantic value; overlapping pixels are merged by a confidence-weighted average.
Confidence Map: cos^2 weighting that decreases with angle from the heading, so centre-of-view pixels are trusted more; overlaps keep confidence-weighted values.
Cost Map: value 1/(dist^k + C) that favors nearer regions and discourages revisiting explored areas.
Optimal-Benefit frontier: frontier score S = mean semantic × mean confidence within radius r around the frontier (cost map fused into the map); argmax frontier is selected.

PEIA: frozen Swin encoder plus multimodal Transformer decoder. Stage 1 pre-trains with discrete prompts (nouns/verbs masked via Flair). Stage 2 fine-tunes only deep continuous prompts (VPT-style), projection and head. Trained on MS COCO captions (0.33M).

RDV: YOLOv7 or Grounding-DINO detection, Mobile-SAM segmentation, VQA check 'Is this <object>?'. A 'no' returns to exploration. A 'yes' triggers point-goal navigation to the centroid of the nearest 25% of points, then STOP. Local navigation uses a depth-only VER-trained point-goal policy.

setting.backbone: PEIA (Swin encoder + multimodal Transformer decoder, prompt-tuned) + Grounding-DINO/YOLOv7 + Mobile-SAM + VQA module + VER point-nav policy
setting.training_data: PEIA pre-trained and prompt-tuned on MS COCO (0.33M); no object-navigation training; VER point-nav policy trained following VLFM
setting.action_space: low-level actions via point-goal navigation to frontiers or object points (STOP within 500 steps, success within 1 m)

numbers.extra: trained only on MS COCO; no ObjectNav training; Table 3/4/5 report SPL 29.06 and DTG 4.09 for the same model
numbers.evidence: Table 1: CoS (Ours) HM3D SPL 29.1, SR 55.9; Tables 2-3: SR 55.90, SPL 29.06, DTG 4.09, NE 10.10

numbers_note: Only the main method is reported; ablation variants on HM3D are in Tables 3-5 and are not listed as separate rows. The paper gives the HM3D val split as 2000 episodes and the MP3D val split as 2195 episodes. The text's '+2.8% vs +2.9% SR over GAMap' is inconsistent, and Table 1 shows 55.9 vs 53.1.
results: CoS reaches 55.9 SR / 29.1 SPL on HM3D and 37.6 SR / 17.6 SPL on MP3D, beating the strongest baselines in SR: UniGoal at 54.5 on HM3D and VLFM at 36.4 on MP3D. SPL on HM3D is below VLFM (30.4), which the authors attribute to more stair travel (6.6 vs 4.6).
limitations: SPL on HM3D is below VLFM (29.1 vs 30.4) and PEIA is weaker than BLIP2 at telling similar frontier observations apart (SPL 29.06 vs 30.31).
MP3D failures are frequently caused by depth near boundaries being set to infinity, which hurts obstacle handling.
Simulation only, with the val splits of two datasets; no real-robot tests or ablations on MP3D.
